query: What customer issues create the most support burden?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: The type/nature of the issue (bug, feature request, how-to) is what generates burden, not a constitutive part of the burden itself. It classifies the source of the problem, not an aspect of how heavy the operational load is.

per_column.name: product_area
per_column.rationale: The product area where the issue arises is a locational attribute of the ticket that may predict or correlate with burden, but it is not an aspect OF the burden concept.

per_column.name: operational_impact
per_column.rationale: Severity of operational impact (outage, degraded performance, data loss) is a genuine constitutive dimension of how much operational burden an issue imposes.

per_column.name: failure_mechanism
per_column.rationale: The underlying technical failure mechanism (regression, race condition, config error) is the causal origin of the issue, not a part of the burden it creates.

per_column.name: affected_user_scope
per_column.rationale: The breadth of users affected (single user to entire/cross tenant) is a real constitutive aspect of burden magnitude -- more affected users means greater burden.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Availability of a workaround directly shapes the ongoing support/operational load a ticket imposes; it is an aspect of the burden's severity/urgency dimension.

per_column.name: escalation_required
per_column.rationale: Whether and what kind of escalation is needed is a direct constitutive aspect of operational burden -- escalation is part of the effort/resource cost the issue imposes.

per_column.name: requires_engineering
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a binary re-encoding of the escalation_required facet (engineering_escalation vs. no_escalation), overlapping heavily with it rather than adding a distinct aspect.

judge.rationale: Operational burden as a concept decomposes into aspects like severity of impact, breadth of affected users, resolvability (workaround), and escalation/effort cost. Four columns (operational_impact, affected_user_scope, workaround_available, escalation_required) qualify as constitutive facets. However, several columns fail the meronymy test: issue_category and failure_mechanism are causes/sources of burden, and product_area is a locational predictor -- none are aspects OF burden. Mutual exclusivity is dragged down because requires_engineering largely restates escalation_required, and escalation/workaround both touch the resolution-effort dimension. Exhaustiveness is moderate: the facet set covers severity, scope, resolvability, and escalation, but omits a direct labor/time-cost dimension (e.g., handling effort, reopen/recurrence, backlog duration) that is core to burden, and it is diluted by the non-facet columns.
